mdmp.title: The seven MDMP steps and their key outputs
mdmp.caption: The seven MDMP steps. The outputs of one step become the inputs of the next; warning orders go out after Steps 1, 2 and 6.

steps.label: Receipt of mission
steps.note: Commander's initial guidance

steps.label: Mission analysis
steps.note: The most critical step: problem statement, mission statement, initial intent and planning guidance, initial CCIRs and EEFIs, COA evaluation criteria

steps.label: COA development
steps.note: Screen each COA: feasible, acceptable, suitable, distinguishable, complete. S3 prepares the COA statement and sketch

steps.label: COA analysis (war game)
steps.note: Action, reaction, counteraction. Belt, avenue-in-depth or box method; no comparing COAs

steps.label: COA comparison
steps.note: Weigh COAs against criteria fixed beforehand; lowest decision-matrix total is most desirable

steps.label: COA approval
steps.note: Commander approves, modifies or rejects; final planning guidance

steps.label: Orders production, dissemination and transition
steps.note: COA statement becomes the concept of operations; S6 prepares Annex H (Signal)

tlp.topic: Steps 1–2: Receive the mission, plan time, and issue a warning order
tlp.title: The eight troop leading procedure steps
tlp.caption: The eight TLP steps. Reverse-plan from the ready time and leave about two-thirds of the available time for subordinates.

steps.label: Receive the mission
steps.note: Work backward from the required ready time

steps.label: Issue a warning order
steps.note: Enough known information for subordinates to start preparing

steps.label: Make a tentative plan
steps.note: Analyze the mission; develop, war-game and compare courses of action

steps.label: Initiate movement
steps.note: Authorized movement can start before the full order

steps.label: Conduct reconnaissance
steps.note: Check information gaps that could alter the tentative plan

steps.label: Complete the plan
steps.note: Integrate reconnaissance findings

steps.label: Issue the order
steps.note: Situation, Mission, Execution, Sustainment, Command and Signal

steps.label: Supervise and refine
steps.note: Backbriefs check plans; rehearsals check coordinated actions; inspections check readiness

signalplanning.title: The signal planning process
signalplanning.caption: Signal planning runs alongside MDMP, or TLP at small-unit level: requirements, real capability, priorities, tentative plan, final checks, publication.

steps.label: Develop requirements
steps.note: Commander's priorities, staff and unit coordination, SOPs, applicable CEOI and CESI

steps.label: Check real capability
steps.note: Equipment readiness, actual personnel fill, training and funds

steps.label: Set priorities
steps.note: When resources are short, rank by supportability and importance to the mission

steps.label: Prepare for disruptions
steps.note: Redundant service, repair or replacement, technical support

steps.label: Prepare the tentative plan
steps.note: Allocate resources; primary, alternate, contingency and emergency support

steps.label: Final checks, then publish
steps.note: Coverage, responsibilities, resources, security, priorities; publish diagrams and instructions with the plans and orders

signalestimate.title: Structure of the signal estimate
signalestimate.caption: METAL organizes the facts; the Annex A estimate then moves from situation to analysis, comparison and recommendation. Revise it when key facts change.

steps.label: Mission
steps.note: Defines what must be supported

steps.label: Enemy signal capabilities
steps.note: Opposing capability

steps.label: Troops available
steps.note: Personnel

steps.label: Area of Operations
steps.note: Operating conditions

steps.label: Logistical requirements
steps.note: Sustainment

steps.label: Situation
steps.note: Terrain, weather, existing communications, opposing and friendly conditions, proposed COAs

steps.label: Analysis
steps.note: What opposing capabilities and limitations mean for friendly support

steps.label: Comparison
steps.note: Options against the same mission requirements

steps.label: Decision and recommendations
steps.note: Personnel, C4S and sustainment; means of communications, command post locations, task list

eccm.title: The enemy's three questions and the EP answer to each
eccm.caption: Found, disrupted, read: each enemy question targets a different risk, so each needs its own protective answer.
rows: Emission control, low power, short transmissions
Frequency hopping, directional antennas, PACE alternate means
Encryption in secure mode, brevity codes, saying less, less often

eccm.topic: EMCON and the need to communicate
eccm.title: EMCON levels 1 to 5
eccm.caption: Emission control levels, from GREEN to the most restrictive BLACK. EMCON 3 AMBER is the field baseline.
eccm.bottom: Most restrictive at the bottom. Rehearse moving between levels.

rungs.name: AMBER
rungs.measures: Encryption, hopping and directional antennas; unencrypted systems off

eccm.title: The example PACE plan
eccm.caption: The lesson's example PACE plan. Know the trigger and rehearse the switch; the alternate follows the primary.

rungs.name: Primary
rungs.measures: Tactical radio in hop and secure mode

rungs.name: Alternate
rungs.measures: HF radio, or another frequency or net

rungs.name: Emergency
rungs.measures: Runner, or visual and pyrotechnic signals

elint.title: Electronic Support compared with ELINT
elint.caption: ES and ELINT can begin with a similar observation; they differ in purpose, user and time horizon.
rows: A tactical commander's immediate awareness needs
Building or updating emitter knowledge, including the Adversary EOB

elint.topic: Read a fingerprint without overclaiming intent
elint.title: Radar signature parameters on a pulse train
elint.caption: Pulse width is duration; the pulse repetition interval is spacing. Several features together give more context than one number.

notes.label: Pulse repetition frequency
notes.note: How often pulses repeat; PRF is the reciprocal of PRI in seconds

notes.label: Carrier frequency
notes.note: Where the signal sits in the spectrum

notes.label: Scan behavior
notes.note: Rotating or sector sweep is consistent with search; a focused pattern with faster repetition can suggest tracking

elint.topic: Read a fingerprint without overclaiming intent
elint.title: Search compared with track
elint.caption: Search and track differ in scan, repetition rate and pulse width. A switch from search to track on the same emitter is reported immediately.
rows: A steady beam held on one target

sigint.topic: Connect requirements, collection, analysis and delivery
sigint.title: The SIGINT cycle from requirement to delivery
sigint.caption: The SIGINT cycle ties collection and analysis to the mission. Direction finding and technical control support the wider process; report what was observed apart from what was assessed.

steps.label: Mission and direction needs
steps.note: Begin with the supported decision or requirement

steps.label: Collect
steps.note: Operators collect relevant material

steps.label: Evaluate
steps.note: Operators evaluate it; keep the observation distinct from the assessment

steps.label: Disseminate
steps.note: Pass the resulting information to those who need it, the intended consumer

intcycle.title: The intelligence cycle
intcycle.caption: The intelligence cycle is dynamic, iterative and continuous.
intcycle.loopLabel: A changed question or new report can prompt renewed collection or analysis.

steps.label: Planning and direction
steps.note: Turn a mission objective into a specific requirement; set priorities

steps.label: Collection
steps.note: HUMINT, SIGINT, IMINT, OSINT

steps.label: Processing and exploitation
steps.note: Translation and data sorting make inputs usable

steps.label: Analysis and production
steps.note: Correlation, pattern and trend analysis; reports with findings and implications

steps.label: Dissemination and integration
steps.note: Deliver to decision-makers; integrate into plans and C2

nist.title: The six CSF Functions
nist.caption: The six Functions. Assign an activity by its immediate purpose; one service can need work in all six at once.

zerotrust.title: Zero Trust core components
zerotrust.caption: Trace a decision from the PE through the PA to the PEP. The PE and PA make up the Policy Decision Point.

steps.label: Policy Engine — decides
steps.note: Grant, deny or revoke access using policy and inputs

steps.label: Policy Administrator — carries out
steps.note: Establishes or closes the path and configures enforcement

steps.label: Policy Enforcement Point — enforces
steps.note: Enables, monitors or terminates the actual connection

cyberrisk.title: From asset to mission risk
cyberrisk.caption: Asset means value, threat means potential harm, and vulnerability means exploitable weakness. Likelihood and mission consequence complete the risk statement.

steps.label: Asset
steps.note: Name it and the confidentiality, integrity or availability it needs

steps.label: Threat
steps.note: Something that could affect the asset

steps.label: Vulnerability
steps.note: The weakness that lets the threat cause harm

steps.label: Likelihood
steps.note: Explain how likely the harm is

steps.label: Mission consequence
steps.note: Explain what the harm means for the mission

cyberrisk.title: The six incident-response phases
cyberrisk.caption: The six incident-response phases. Review records findings for improvement.
cyberrisk.loopLabel: Findings from assessment and review feed improvement.

steps.label: Preparation
steps.note: Readies people, tools and procedures

steps.label: Identification
steps.note: Detects and recognizes incidents

steps.label: Containment
steps.note: Limits spread; the cause can still be present

steps.label: Eradication
steps.note: Removes incident components and validates the cleanup

steps.label: Recovery
steps.note: Restores healthy service

steps.label: Assessment and review
steps.note: Records findings for improvement

ethicalleadership.topic: Six steps for an ethical decision
ethicalleadership.title: Six steps for an ethical decision
ethicalleadership.caption: Define, know the rules, develop options, evaluate, decide and act, reflect. Compare alternatives explicitly before acting.

steps.label: Define the dilemma
steps.note: Identify the duties or values in tension

steps.label: Know the rules
steps.note: Laws, orders, regulations and values that apply

steps.label: Develop options
steps.note: Generate feasible courses of action

steps.label: Evaluate
steps.note: Test each for legal, moral and mission implications

steps.label: Decide and act
steps.note: Take responsibility for the action

steps.label: Reflect
steps.note: Learn from the outcome and prevent recurrence

weapons.title: The D3A cycle
weapons.caption: D3A presents Decide, Detect, Deliver and Assess as distinct functions in a cycle. Decision authority remains with the command function.
weapons.loopLabel: Assess evaluates what happened after delivery, and the cycle continues.

steps.label: Assess
steps.note: Evaluates what happened after delivery

missioncommand.title: Choosing the degree of control
missioncommand.caption: Control is a sliding choice, and it can vary by decision within a single task.

left.title: Tighter control when…
items: The consequences of an error are severe

right.title: More judgment when…
items: Competence and mutual trust have grown

missioncommand.note: Adjust oversight as trust, competence, risk, time, environment and complexity change.

signal.title: From signal estimate to updated support
signal.caption: A shortfall drives the priority recommendation. Apply COMSEC and network protection to the paths chosen for both normal service and recovery.

steps.label: Signal estimate
steps.note: Assesses operational requirements and usable resources

steps.label: Priority recommendation
steps.note: A shortfall in resources drives it

steps.label: Tentative plan
steps.note: Coordinated with the operations staff and the units that will execute it

steps.label: Publication
steps.note: Gives users a common arrangement

steps.label: Update
steps.note: Preserves alignment as the mission changes; confirm users understand revised and alternate arrangements

c4istarplanning.title: Following a report from source to display
c4istarplanning.caption: Follow a report from source to display to locate a failed handoff; identify where an error first appears in the chain.

steps.label: Sensors and reconnaissance systems
steps.note: Produce observations

steps.label: Networks
steps.note: Carry the data

steps.label: Databases and computing resources
steps.note: Support storage and processing

steps.label: Analytical tools
steps.note: Help extract insights

steps.label: Command consoles and operations centers
steps.note: Use information for coordination and decisions
